jobs.title: CSST/Staff Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description:
We have an immediate opening in our Irvine, California office for a Senior Staff Environmental Scientist with a CSST and hazardous materials/industrial hygiene experience (required).

Duties will include:
Making frequent visits to project sites at the direction of the Project Manager.
Acquiring permits, and reviewing background data, site photos and aerial photographs.
Assist the Project Manager in the acquisition, documentation and dissemination of data related to all phases of environmental assessment/projects. These activities will include, but not be limited to, performing site reconnaissance, asbestos and lead surveys, abatement monitoring, industrial hygiene evaluations.
Preparation of field data, photographic documentation, and quantification of hazardous materials.
Performing various assigned tasks such as coordinating and scheduling subcontractors, performing basic calculations, preparing field studies, and report writing under the direction of the Project Manager.
Perform assignments of limited scope and complexity, usually as a portion of broader assignments, in accordance with established company policies/procedures.
Conduct special assignments as directed by the supervisor.

Education:
A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or related scientific field or technical field from an accredited institution is required.

Required Certifications:
Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) or CAC & and Lead Inspector/Assessor/Project Monitor/Sampling Technician REQUIRED

Required skills:

At least two years of professional work experience performing most or all of the duties listed in the job description (at least under number 3)
Ability to perform fieldwork, data collection, evaluation, and technical writing skills.
Good written and verbal communication, analytical, organizational and time management skills are required.
Ability to work collaboratively and with discretion.
Attention to detail, integrity, organization, communication, interpersonal, clerical, and computer skills.
Basic knowledge of computer software pertaining to environmental design.
Ability to carry out fieldwork at times in hazardous conditions because of climate isolation, topography, or means of transportation.
Valid driver’s license with acceptable violation history.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
An exciting career awaits you

At MPC, we’re committed to being a great place to work – one that welcomes new ideas, encourages diverse perspectives, develops our people, and fosters a collaborative team environment.

The Logistics & Storage Environmental, Safety, Security and Product Quality (L&S ESS&PQ) department is seeking an enthusiastic, collaborative professional ready to expand their technical expertise, influence business decisions, and grow as an environmental leader. We are looking for candidates who build strong partnerships across teams, communicate effectively in both speaking and writing, and thrive in a fast-paced environment where their work can make a visible impact.

Position Summary:

The MPLX L&S ESS&PQ Group has a full-time, exempt opening for an Air Subject Matter Expert (SME) on the Air Compliance and Technical Support Team. This highly visible role will lead environmental air permitting and air compliance efforts for terminals, pipeline and marine facilities, and transport fleets across the country. The position offers an opportunity to shape compliance strategy, guide complex projects, build broad organizational relationships, and develop leadership capabilities while becoming a trusted technical advisor to the business.

Candidate location is flexible and can be based at any L&S location. This position may require up to 25% travel with occasional overnight stays.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as a key member of an experienced team of Air SMEs, with opportunities to lead initiatives, broaden technical expertise, and influence environmental strategy. Responsibilities will include the following:

Serving as a trusted advisor to field Environmental Specialists by providing day-to-day air permitting and regulatory compliance support.

Leading and supporting implementation of new and revised air regulations (i.e., 40 CFR Part 60 Subpart XXa and Part 63 Subparts R and BBBBBB).

Collaborating with, and providing support and backup for, other Air SMEs (e.g., storage tanks, CEMS, LDAR), creating opportunities to expand expertise across multiple programs.

Performing and documenting New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) determinations for terminal, pipeline, and marine projects.

Leading and supporting air permit and compliance audits, communicating insights to stakeholders, and driving continuous improvement through the internal auditing program.

Representing L&S in rule advocacy efforts through trade organizations, such as the International Liquid Terminals Association (ILTA), and helping shape practical regulatory outcomes.

Creating and improving guidance documents and compliance tools that establish consistent practices and enable effective decision-making across the organization.

Developing and delivering training to field Environmental Specialists on a wide range of air compliance and permitting topics, strengthening technical capability across the team.

Helping lead emerging technology evaluations and digital transformation initiatives, such as Next Gen Maintenance and the new Environmental Accounting & Tasking system.
Serve as Air Permitting Coordinator for the L&S organization — a visible leadership assignment that connects environmental expertise with engineering, operations, business development, and senior stakeholders.

Represent L&S Environmental in engineering, business development, and other project-related meetings, providing clear recommendations and helping teams navigate permitting and scope decisions.

Own and advance the air permit and project tracking program.

Set air permitting priorities and strategically align internal and external resources.

Identify the timeliest and most cost-effective permitting pathways to support project schedules and business objectives.

Provide clear, proactive project updates — including scope changes and permit timing — to stakeholders and leadership.

Lead or support development of air permit applications, complete detailed reviews of draft permits, and recommend solutions to complex permitting issues.

Build productive relationships with state agencies and Field Environmental Specialists to obtain permits that support business objectives.

Develop into a recognized Air Permitting SME for New Source Review (NSR), Title V (major), and non-Title V (minor) permitting, with a pathway to broader technical and organizational leadership.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or GED required with 15 years of relevant environmental experience in a process industry (e.g. refining, midstream, petrochemical or other heavy industrial); or Bachelor’s degree in a HES related field, Engineering degree, or advanced degree with 7 years relevant environmental experience.
Detailed knowledge on current and proposed environmental rules and regulations with the ability to communicate impact plans to local leadership for budget development.
Ability to review engineering designs and specifications to ensure compliance with appropriate environmental rules and regulations.
Comprehensive knowledge of facilities and relationships with environmental rules and regulations with the ability to initiate steps that will avoid reoccurrence of environmental problems.
A driver’s license is required.
Must possess or be able to obtain a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC).

Preferred Qualifications
:

At least 5 years of air permitting and compliance experience is preferred.
Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering, or Environmental Management is preferred.
Relevant industry certifications are preferred.
Strong background in environmental compliance related to oil and gas operations is preferred.

As an energy industry leader, our career opportunities fuel personal and professional growth.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
Our client is seeking an experienced Environmental Compliance Manager
to support environmental compliance activities across multiple projects and operating facilities throughout California.

This position will combine environmental leadership with hands-on technical compliance responsibilities. The Environmental Compliance Manager will support projects through various stages of development, construction, and operations while working closely with internal project teams, field personnel, consultants, and regulatory agencies.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in environmental permitting and compliance within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or another highly regulated environment. This individual should be comfortable interpreting complex environmental requirements, providing direction to others, managing multiple priorities, and ensuring compliance requirements are effectively implemented in the field.

Responsibilities

Lead and coordinate environmental compliance activities across multiple project and operational sites.
Provide technical guidance and direction to environmental personnel, consultants, contractors, and project teams.
Support environmental compliance throughout pre-construction, construction, and ongoing operations.
Review environmental permits, plans, mitigation measures, and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical field requirements.
Oversee field inspections, compliance documentation, regulatory reporting, corrective actions, and permit obligations.
Support compliance programs involving stormwater and water quality, wildlife and biological resources, spill prevention, air quality, hazardous materials, and waste.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies and support agency inspections, meetings, and compliance responses.
Track environmental commitments, permit conditions, reporting deadlines, corrective actions, and other compliance obligations.
Review environmental reports, field documentation, regulatory submissions, and technical work products.
Coordinate environmental consultants and technical service providers.
Develop practical environmental procedures, training materials, checklists, and field tools.
Identify potential environmental compliance risks and work with internal stakeholders to develop appropriate corrective and preventive actions.
Support environmental permitting and due diligence activities associated with new and existing projects.
Maintain organized and accurate environmental compliance records.
Travel to project and operating sites throughout California as needed.

﻿

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Natural Resources, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or a comparable environment.
Experience leading environmental programs, projects, field teams, or environmental professionals.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience interpreting environmental permits and implementing requirements in active field environments.
Experience with construction and/or operational environmental compliance.
Knowledge of stormwater/SWPPP, spill prevention, hazardous materials and waste, air quality, water quality, and environmental permitting.
Experience with wildlife, biological resources, mitigation monitoring, and resource agency permitting is highly desirable.
Experience interacting with regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple sites, deadlines, and priorities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while providing leadership and direction to others.
Ability to travel regularly throughout California, including occasional overnight travel.

jobs.title: Air Quality Managing Consultant - Western Region
jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

ALL4 is seeking an experienced Air Quality Managing Consultant
with experience in air quality and other environmental media to support projects in the Western Region of United States (U.S.)
. An ALL4 Managing Consultant is an air quality technical expert who shares our vision and passion for helping our clients be successful. They are self-motivated, coachable, growth-oriented individuals who can build client relationships, successfully manage complex projects and teams, and identify business opportunities with existing and new clients. The ALL4 Managing Consultant works closely with clients in a strategic partnership supported by a foundation of authentic communication, personal ownership, and accountability. This individual will join a team of environmental professionals that are well-versed in complex permitting, compliance, and modeling projects, and who are committed to furthering our vision as a globally recognized consulting company shaping environmental responsibility and creating distinction for employees, clients, and partners. This role offers flexibility to work at any of ALL4's U.S. office locations. For individuals not near an ALL4 office, this role can be performed fully remote.

Requirements

Plan, manage, and execute all relevant project tasks, including developing project proposals and plans to determine time frame, budget, allotment of resources, and procedures for executing and completing multiple projects across industries, while serving as clients’ primary point of contact.
Prepare and execute high-level technical and consulting work and direct others on how to do the same.
Monitor and control project activities to achieve project milestones and financial performance objectives.
Effectively and proactively communicate project information to the team.
Cultivate and lead projects already under contract and expand business with existing clients.
Manage annual client revenues as collaboratively determined by the leadership team.
Prioritize client engagement through routine and repeating outreach, in-person connection, and intentional sharing of ALL4 services and capabilities.
Meet ALL4 profitability targets and personal utilization goals.
Review client invoices consistent with established schedule and ensure project opening and closing documentation is completed consistent with established schedule.
Establish and maintain relationships with regulatory organizations and provide interpretation, review, and strategic analysis of federal, state, and local environmental regulations to clients.
Implement and monitor project procedures to ensure the quality of project deliverables and attainment of contractual agreements.
Ensure compliance of projects with ALL4 quality assurance guidelines.
Manage health and safety component of project fieldwork (e.g., development of onsite health and safety plan).
Conduct regular meetings with the project team on status of work.
Exhibit ALL4’s core values in all transactions (internally and externally) and mentor junior technical staff.
Potentially coordinate staff.
Demonstrate a high level of professionalism regarding confidential and sensitive issues.
Perform other related duties as assigned by management.

Qualifications

Engineering or applicable environmental/science degree and collective experiences equivalent to a minimum of 5 years of Environmental consulting experience.
Working knowledge of technical subjects impacting air permitting (e.g., NSR, minor NSR, Title V, TRI, Tier II, SPCC, NPDES, and SWPPP).
Established relationships with regulatory agencies and/or industrial sector professionals.
Commitment to excellence and ALL4’s core values; openness to change, personal growth, and coaching.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and analytical skills; able to manage priorities and workflow proactively; demonstrated project management ability.
Ability to develop, lead, and enroll strong teams with a wide range of personality types and technical abilities.
Effective problem resolution combined with the ability to delegate effectively.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including strong document production skills (proficiency in Word and Excel) and technical writing ability.
Acute attention to detail.

About ALL4

ALL4 is a leading provider of strategic consulting services, helping organizations navigate complex Environmental, Health, and Safety challenges across a broad range of heavily regulated industries including, but not limited to, pulp and paper, food and beverage, consumer products, data centers, cement, healthcare, chemical, pharmaceutical, transportation, waste management, higher education, power, oil and gas, and automotive.

Our areas of expertise encompass air quality, chemical reporting and management, digital solutions, sustainability, investigation and remediation, environmental planning and permitting, occupational health and safety, waste management, and water quality. With offices and remote experts across the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Spain, Chile, and Brazil, ALL4 brings a robust North American presence and a growing international footprint—positioning us to support clients seamlessly and effectively around the world.

ALL4 operates from key offices in the metropolitan areas of Philadelphia, PA (headquarters); Rancho Cucamonga, CA; San Juan Capistrano, CA; Washington, D.C.; Gainesville, FL; Atlanta, GA; Lexington, KY; Louisville, KY; Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; Houston, TX; Bellingham, WA; and Madrid, Spain.

ALL4 Has Consistently Earned Recognition As a “Best Place To Work” Both Regionally And Nationally, Reflecting Its Growth In Personnel, Culture, And Environmental Impact. Notable Honors Include

Verdantix Green Quadrant for service providers – Innovator Status
Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Companies
ENR Top 200 Environmental Firms
Zweig Hot Firm – Fastest Growing Firms
Best Companies Group

We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

jobs.title: Service Center Supervisor- Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Bend, OR
jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West is seeking a Service Center Supervisor to join our team in Bend OR!

Responsibilities

Oversee all activities and employees of the location
Project management of all received samples and projects as needed
Analyze microbiology and inorganic testing on potable and non-potable water samples
Perform monthly environmental testing (water, surfaces, air) and annual calibrations
Receive and log potable water and non-potable water samples from clients
Create microbiological and chemical projects and reports and corresponding invoices
Prepare various media types for sample analysis
Submit all compliance drinking water to Oregon State Heath Authority and EPA as needed
Answer and respond to all client correspondence via phone and email
Schedule all equipment calibration and maintain diligent records
Schedule all sample collections performed by the location
Consult public on testing and sampling procedures
Consult water systems and utilities on testing and sampling procedures
Maintain laboratory supply inventory
Maintain all SOPs and training documents
Maintain all NELAP certification requirements including but not limited to: proficiency testing, internal audits, logbook audits, on-site audits by accreditation body and audit responses
Act as onsite Quality Control Officer
Maintain and organize clients chemical and sampling schedules along with bottle orders and personalized CoCs.
Ability to analyze samples on weekends, holidays and on call, as needed

Qualifications

Skills/Qualifications

Aseptic technique
Excellent customer service
Reliable, timely and punctual
Multitasking with strong time management
Work within strict time requirements of microbiology tests
Excellent documentation, computer and organization skills
Must be able to communicate effectively with lab personnel and clients
Previous knowledge of environmental testing and compliance regulations is desired

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, biology, or equivalent
2 years customer experience preferred
Minimum of two weeks training at academic institution in microbiological analysis of drinking water or 80 hours on the job training

Additional Information

Position is full-time salaried, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of longer hours and weekends as needed.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 - $70,000 annually.

Candidates within a commutable distance to Bend, OR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description
: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in environmental permitting and compliance within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or another highly regulated environment. This individual should be comfortable interpreting complex environmental requirements, providing direction to others, managing multiple priorities, and ensuring compliance requirements are effectively implemented in the field.

Responsibilities

Lead and coordinate environmental compliance activities across multiple project and operational sites.
Provide technical guidance and direction to environmental personnel, consultants, contractors, and project teams.
Support environmental compliance throughout pre-construction, construction, and ongoing operations.
Review environmental permits, plans, mitigation measures, and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical field requirements.
Oversee field inspections, compliance documentation, regulatory reporting, corrective actions, and permit obligations.
Support compliance programs involving stormwater and water quality, wildlife and biological resources, spill prevention, air quality, hazardous materials, and waste.
Coordinate with regulatory and resource agencies and support agency inspections, meetings, and compliance responses.
Track environmental commitments, permit conditions, reporting deadlines, corrective actions, and other compliance obligations.
Review environmental reports, field documentation, regulatory submissions, and technical work products.
Coordinate environmental consultants and technical service providers.
Develop practical environmental procedures, training materials, checklists, and field tools.
Identify potential environmental compliance risks and work with internal stakeholders to develop appropriate corrective and preventive actions.
Support environmental permitting and due diligence activities associated with new and existing projects.
Maintain organized and accurate environmental compliance records.
Travel to project and operating sites throughout California as needed.

﻿

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Natural Resources, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive environmental compliance experience within energy, construction, infrastructure, industrial operations, or a comparable environment.
Experience leading environmental programs, projects, field teams, or environmental professionals.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience interpreting environmental permits and implementing requirements in active field environments.
Experience with construction and/or operational environmental compliance.
Knowledge of stormwater/SWPPP, spill prevention, hazardous materials and waste, air quality, water quality, and environmental permitting.
Experience with wildlife, biological resources, mitigation monitoring, and resource agency permitting is highly desirable.
Experience interacting with regulatory agencies and environmental consultants.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple sites, deadlines, and priorities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while providing leadership and direction to others.
Ability to travel regularly throughout California, including occasional overnight travel.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West is seeking a Service Center Supervisor to join our team in Bend OR!

Responsibilities

Oversee all activities and employees of the location
Project management of all received samples and projects as needed
Analyze microbiology and inorganic testing on potable and non-potable water samples
Perform monthly environmental testing (water, surfaces, air) and annual calibrations
Receive and log potable water and non-potable water samples from clients
Create microbiological and chemical projects and reports and corresponding invoices
Prepare various media types for sample analysis
Submit all compliance drinking water to Oregon State Heath Authority and EPA as needed
Answer and respond to all client correspondence via phone and email
Schedule all equipment calibration and maintain diligent records
Schedule all sample collections performed by the location
Consult public on testing and sampling procedures
Consult water systems and utilities on testing and sampling procedures
Maintain laboratory supply inventory
Maintain all SOPs and training documents
Maintain all NELAP certification requirements including but not limited to: proficiency testing, internal audits, logbook audits, on-site audits by accreditation body and audit responses
Act as onsite Quality Control Officer
Maintain and organize clients chemical and sampling schedules along with bottle orders and personalized CoCs.
Ability to analyze samples on weekends, holidays and on call, as needed

Qualifications

Skills/Qualifications

Aseptic technique
Excellent customer service
Reliable, timely and punctual
Multitasking with strong time management
Work within strict time requirements of microbiology tests
Excellent documentation, computer and organization skills
Must be able to communicate effectively with lab personnel and clients
Previous knowledge of environmental testing and compliance regulations is desired

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, biology, or equivalent
2 years customer experience preferred
Minimum of two weeks training at academic institution in microbiological analysis of drinking water or 80 hours on the job training

Additional Information

Position is full-time salaried, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of longer hours and weekends as needed.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 - $70,000 annually.

Candidates within a commutable distance to Bend, OR are encouraged to apply.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description
: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.
